payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Change the black DVD to white while retaining its identity as a DVD.
node.criteria: Judge only the requested transformation, using both support observations. Return yes when the DVD is visibly white rather than black and retains its identity as a DVD. Return no only when there is sufficient evidence that no requested change has progressed—for example, the DVD remains black and retains its identity. Return partial when the color change has progressed but the DVD is not yet white, or when the DVD is white but its identity as a DVD has been lost. Unrelated edits do not count. If the evidence does not establish one of these outcomes, return unresolved. Support observations are evidence, not independent completion credit.
node.binding: Target: The DVD is visibly white rather than black.. Reference: The black DVD in the input image..

response.content: {"text":"The node’s binding is too vague and its traces appear to accept a white disc anywhere as the target. In the images, the original DVD is the small rectangular item near the center; the edited image shows two white discs, while the original item is no longer clearly identifiable at that location. Do not infer that the DVD was recolored merely because white discs are visible or because a disc-shaped object has a center hole. Tighten target binding to track the specific original DVD across the edit, and require evidence that this same object changed from black to white and retained DVD identity. Evaluate the joint requested transformation using the support observations, distinguishing complete fulfillment from partial progress or no progress; do not treat support checks as independent completion credit. The repeated high-confidence “yes” traces suggest a systematic target-correspondence/evidence problem, not uncertainty to resolve by lowering confidence. The reference “no” is an aggregate constraint, not atomic ground truth: inspect whether the original target remains unchanged, is missing/obscured, or has been replaced, and use unresolved when the images do not establish the outcome. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated."}
